title: Cut repeats before content
statement: When a lesson feels long, cut its redundant repeats, such as an answer shown twice, before any content, but keep deliberate returns like a framing line.
example: One prototype lesson showed its learning question three times.
detail: A review of a Grade 9 lesson prototype counted its repeats: the same six words introduced on two screens, the learning question three times and the answer twice. It judged each one small, but together a large part of why the lesson felt long, and cutting them cheaper than cutting content. Its checklist made an audit for repeated content, and explaining the program once at first open instead of again in every unit, priority items. The unit's film script kept a statement made in both its first and eighth scenes, calling it a frame, not the repetition the review objected to (`g9/library/text/L5d411f.txt`, line 23).
against: The same review separates a lesson that is long from one that only feels long: "Twenty-eight steps each doing distinct work is a session-length decision. Twenty-eight where several feel similar is redundancy, and the fix is cutting or merging" (`g9/sources/Othello_1_Feedback_DevFactory.md`, line 202). Cutting repeats answers a lesson that feels long, not one that is long.
